issues.t: Timing chain rattle from worn tensioners and guides
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, especially at cold start, a check engine light with camshaft timing codes, or rough running.
issues.why: On the 5.0L V8 the steel tensioner pistons wear grooves into the aluminum-backed chain guides, letting the chains go slack. If the timing jumps, valves can be damaged.
issues.next: Don't ignore a start-up rattle. Have the codes read and the timing components inspected; replacing guides and tensioners before a chain jumps avoids engine damage.

issues.t: Fuel smell from cracked fuel tank flange (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell inside or around the car, especially in the garage, or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: The plastic outlet flange on top of the fuel tank can crack and leak. Jaguar ran several recalls (including NHTSA 12V521 for 5.0L cars and 20V081 for 2010 4.2L cars), and some owners report the same failure on cars outside the recall.
issues.next: Any fuel smell is a fire risk. Park outside, check your VIN for open recalls, and have the tank flange inspected right away.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a crash the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: These cars used Takata passenger airbag inflators whose propellant breaks down with heat and humidity. Jaguar recalled them in several campaigns (including NHTSA 16V373, 17V027 and 18V010).
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA's site or with a Jaguar dealer and get the free replacement done as soon as possible.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The driver airbag may deploy improperly in a crash.
issues.why: Some driver airbag modules built from 2008 to 2014 lacked a chemical needed for second-stage deployment. Jaguar recalled certain 2009, 2011, 2012 and 2015 cars (NHTSA 16V229).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the module replaced free at a dealer.

issues.t: Rotary gear selector won't rise or turn
issues.sym: The round gear selector knob stays down at start-up or won't rotate, so you can't select Drive or Reverse. It can also drop back down unexpectedly.
issues.why: Jaguar issued bulletins for the rotary transmission control switch failing to rise or rotate on 2009-2013 cars. Owners have reported the knob retracting while driving.
issues.next: Try restarting the car with your foot firmly on the brake. If it keeps happening, have the selector module diagnosed; it may need a replacement unit or software.

issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a low coolant message, a sweet smell, or the engine overheating.
issues.why: Water pumps are the most replaced part reported by XF owners. Jaguar issued a bulletin for coolant leaks from the 5.0L V8 water pump.
issues.next: Top up coolant only with the correct type and have the pump checked. Stop driving if the temperature gauge rises.

issues.t: Water pump failure on supercharged V6
issues.sym: Coolant leaks, a low coolant warning, a whining or grinding noise from the front of the engine, or overheating. Some fail before 20,000 miles.
issues.why: On the 3.0L supercharged V6, coolant can seep into the water pump bearing and rust it. Water pumps top owner repair reports for the XF.
issues.next: Have the pump inspected at the first sign of a leak or noise. The pump is at the front of the engine and is one of the easier jobs on this car.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from expansion tank or coolant pipes
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, coolant smell, or wet patches under the engine.
issues.why: Jaguar issued bulletins for leaking coolant expansion tanks and a leak at the seam of a V8 coolant pipe. Hoses, pipes and the expansion tank are among the most replaced XF parts.
issues.next: Have a cooling-system pressure test to find the leak and fix it before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Supercharger rattle at idle
issues.sym: A clatter, knock or rattle from the top front of the engine, most noticeable at idle.
issues.why: Jaguar described wear in the supercharger drive isolator that adds backlash in the drive. If the rotors or bearings are also worn, the whole supercharger has to be replaced.
issues.next: Have a specialist confirm where the noise comes from. Fitting the isolator kit early can avoid a full supercharger replacement.

issues.t: Dashboard leather bubbling or shrinking
issues.sym: The leather on the top of the dashboard bubbles, lifts or pulls away from the edges.
issues.why: The dash covering separates from its backing, mostly on cars parked in hot sun. Owners have filed many complaints about it.
issues.next: Use a sunshade and ask a dealer about goodwill help. Fixing it means re-covering or replacing the dash top.

issues.t: Engine shutting off while driving
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning, sometimes at highway speed, with warning lights on the dash.
issues.why: Owners of 2010 cars filed many stalling complaints, and Jaguar issued an engine-management update for cut-outs at low speed and bulletins for stalling after a hot soak.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer to safety. Have the codes read and ask a dealer to confirm the latest engine software is installed.

issues.t: Hard starting or rough idle from clogged injectors
issues.sym: Long cranking, rough running or a stall right after a hot restart, misfires, or a check engine light.
issues.why: Jaguar issued bulletins for clogged fuel injectors on the V8 and for rough starts after a hot soak on the 4.2L engine.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Injector cleaning or replacement and a software update are the usual fixes.

issues.t: Battery drain and charging warnings
issues.sym: A dead battery after the car sits, a charging warning light, or odd electrical faults.
issues.why: Jaguar issued bulletins for battery discharge and charging warnings, including a negative battery cable that can work loose.
issues.next: Have the battery, cable connections and charging system tested. Keep the battery on a maintainer if the car sits for long periods.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning from compressor clutch
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only cools some of the time.
issues.why: Jaguar issued several bulletins on poor A/C performance traced to the compressor clutch.
issues.next: Have the A/C system diagnosed; the clutch can sometimes be fixed without replacing the whole compressor.

issues.t: Touchscreen and Bluetooth glitches
issues.sym: The touchscreen goes blank or reboots, Bluetooth drops calls or won't pair, and the radio or parking camera stops working.
issues.why: Jaguar issued several bulletins for Bluetooth pairing and software problems, and owners report the screen and audio cutting out.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to update the infotainment software. A battery reset sometimes helps for a while.

issues.t: LED tail lights failing from corrosion
issues.sym: A bulb failure warning or sections of the rear LED lights not working.
issues.why: Jaguar issued bulletins for rear LED lamps failing due to corrosion. Tail light assemblies are commonly replaced on the XF.
issues.next: Check the lights and have the lamp assembly replaced; the LEDs aren't serviceable separately.

issues.t: Rusty rear subframe
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear or visible heavy rust on the rear subframe.
issues.why: Corroded subframes are a known first-generation XF problem.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift, especially in salt-belt states.

issues.t: Transfer case flange oil leak on AWD cars
issues.sym: Oil drips under the middle of the car or an oily film near the transfer case.
issues.why: Jaguar issued a bulletin for oil leaking from the transfer case flange on all-wheel-drive XF and XJ models.
issues.next: Have the leak checked and the oil level topped up so the transfer case isn't damaged.

issues.t: Rear differential pinion seal leak
issues.sym: Oil on the rear differential or drips under the back of the car, sometimes with a whine.
issues.why: Jaguar issued a bulletin for oil leaks at the rear differential pinion seal. Axle and output seals are commonly replaced on the XF.
issues.next: Have the seal replaced and the differential oil topped up before it runs low.

issues.t: Coolant and oil leaks around the supercharger
issues.sym: Coolant or oil smell, low coolant warnings, or leaks near the top or back of the engine.
issues.why: On the 3.0L supercharged V6, coolant pipes under the supercharger crack, and the oil cooler and intake manifold gaskets fail.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Repairs under the supercharger take many hours, so ask for a written estimate.

issues.t: Timing chain wear on 2.0L diesel
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine, a check engine light, or a low oil warning.
issues.why: The 2.0L Ingenium four-cylinder diesel is known for timing chain problems, and low oil warnings sometimes appeared while internal damage was already happening.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and changed on time. Have any rattle checked right away; chain replacement on this engine is a big job.

issues.t: Door lock actuator failure
issues.sym: A door won't lock or unlock with the remote or the button, or the alarm acts up.
issues.why: Door lock actuators fail on this generation and are among the most replaced XF parts.
issues.next: Have the actuator replaced; it is inside the door.

issues.t: Water leaking into cabin or trunk
issues.sym: Damp carpets in the cabin or water collecting in the trunk.
issues.why: Owners report water leaks that soak carpets in the cabin and boot, and Jaguar issued a bulletin for water getting into the trunk.
issues.next: Look under the trunk floor and carpets for water. Have the seals and drains checked before wiring and modules corrode.

issues.t: Infotainment freezing and Bluetooth drops
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, the navigation is slow or crashes, and phone calls drop over Bluetooth.
issues.why: The InControl Touch Pro system on these cars is known for software glitches. Jaguar issued updates, but complaints are common.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to install the latest software. A full system restart can clear a frozen screen for now.

issues.t: Weak 12V battery causing random faults
issues.sym: Several warning messages at once, features that stop working, or a car that won't start.
issues.why: These cars draw a lot of power from the 12V battery, and a weak battery can trigger a range of faults.
issues.next: Have the battery tested before chasing other faults. Use a battery maintainer if the car isn't driven often.

issues.t: Hooting noise from transmission cooler pipes
issues.sym: A low owl-like hoot at low speed.
issues.why: The transmission oil cooler pipework can resonate. Revised foam pads in the cooler bracket can reduce it.
issues.next: It is not harmful, but a dealer can fit the revised pads.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital instrument display goes dark while driving, hiding speed and warnings.
issues.why: A software fault in the 12.3-inch virtual instrument cluster. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 17V678) for a software update.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the update installed.

issues.t: Cracked sill could rupture fuel lines (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. A cracked left inner sill could let fuel lines rupture in a side impact.
issues.why: Some 2017 cars had cracks in the left inner sill panel. Under recall NHTSA 17V084, cars with cracks were bought back and replaced.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and contact a Jaguar dealer.

issues.t: Fuel rail end caps leaking (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: Fuel rail end caps on the 2.0L gasoline engine can leak fuel near hot engine parts. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 18V090) to replace the fuel rail.
issues.next: Any fuel smell is a fire risk. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the work done right away.

issues.t: Airbags may deploy incorrectly on Sportbrake (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The front airbags may deploy the wrong way in a low-speed crash.
issues.why: An incorrect airbag system calibration on the XF Sportbrake wagon. Jaguar recalled them (NHTSA 18V112) for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the update done.

issues.t: Seat belt may not secure a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat may not stay tight when installed with the seat belt.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor in the seat belt can switch off too early. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 21V667) to inspect and replace belts.
issues.next: Use the LATCH anchors for child seats until the recall is done, and contact a dealer.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioners may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The front belts may not tighten properly in a crash.
issues.why: The driver and front passenger seat belt pretensioners may be damaged. Jaguar recalled these cars (NHTSA 22V524) to inspect and replace belts as needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and book the free repair.
